HyLight raises €13 million to expand autonomous inspection airships

The company targets a fleet increase from four to 15 while expanding AI analysis and European operations.

Tech.eu ↗12 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Funding inspection services

French company HyLight raised €13 million from Rubio Impact Ventures, DRW and Teampact Ventures alongside existing investors. Its hydrogen-powered airships inspect power lines, pipelines and railways, with a target of 15 aircraft by 2027 versus four today.

Endurance and sensing

The 12-metre HyLighter is specified for up to ten hours of flight and ten kilograms of sensors, including LiDAR, cameras and methane detectors. The company says its analysis locates vegetation risks and more than 50 types of power-grid defects.

Scaling an integrated service

HyLight builds and operates its aircraft and supplies analysis to customers including Enedis, NaTran, Téréga, SNCF Réseau and VINCI. Funding supports manufacturing, hiring and markets such as Germany and the Netherlands; 15 aircraft remains a target and flights require applicable permissions.
